payload.exact_statement: For every feasible cell vector x in the baseline model, there is a finite-piece measurable history with each a_ijr in {0,1} and sum_ir a_ijr<=1 for every person, preserving every stream cell integral and every cell-linear target. Partition each person-cell consecutively into stream blocks of lengths x_ijrk and an idle remainder. Conversely these histories are admissible, hence their feasible cell/target sets equal the baseline sets. This requires arbitrary preemption and no minimum-session, switching, synchronisation or extra pointwise constraints; it does not imply integral cell totals.
payload.proof: For each j,k order streams and assign stream s the half-open interval from b_(k-1)+sum_(t<s)x_tjk to b_(k-1)+sum_(t<=s)x_tjk. Capacity fits these disjoint blocks in the cell. Their lengths are exactly x; all observations and targets are sums of these preserved integrals. Binary histories are a subset of fractional histories.
payload.aggregation_statement: Within each fixed person-cell capacity block, merge only variables with identical columns across all observation and retained target rows. Their sum is the aggregate variable; lifting all mass to one representative proves exact equality of feasible target sets, infeasibility and extrema. Include any additional individual constraints in the signature/lift.
payload.network_counterexample: One person, one [0,2] cell, streams A,B,C, observations A+B=A+C=B+C=1: matrix determinant -2, unique x=(1/2,1/2,1/2), sum=3/2<=2. Thus the arbitrary-group observation matrix is not automatically TU and integral-data cell totals need not be integral. This refutes a blanket original-matrix integral-flow claim, not all possible extended network representations.
payload.recommendation: Retain joint LP. Adopt serial attainment corollary and narrow claim that fractional instantaneous allocations are necessary; optionally use equal-column preprocessing. Reject unproved pooling, no-interruption restriction and universal graph replacement.
